selection_rationale: Germany is the largest missing country-level context in the European research layer. Existing work covers France, the Eurosystem, Russia and daily euro-area macro signals but lacks a reusable dossier connecting Germany's export-industrial system, federal institutions, infrastructure financing shift, energy transition, defence rearmament and demographic labour constraint.
contrary_evidence: Germany retains exceptional industrial density, a large skilled workforce, high savings, deep EU market access and a persistent external surplus, arguing against a simple deindustrialization or decline thesis.

Larger fiscal authorizations and renewable capacity do not by themselves establish higher productivity or lower delivered industrial energy costs; execution, grids, private investment and sectoral restructuring remain binding.
limitations: The 2026 GDP, employment and fiscal data are point-in-time observations and will be revised.
Official defence totals differ by budgetary, constitutional and NATO accounting definitions and should not be mechanically combined.
National averages obscure large differences across Länder, industrial clusters and municipalities.
Long-run population projections are conditional scenarios rather than deterministic outcomes.

en.title: Germany: export-industrial depth, federal bargaining and the fiscal-energy transition of Europe's largest economy
en.deck: Germany retains exceptional industrial depth and institutional capacity, but its 2026 transition depends on converting larger infrastructure, defence and energy investment into productivity while employment and demography tighten.
en.regime: Industrial conversion under fiscal expansion: export manufacturing, federal institutions and deep savings coexist with weaker employment, demographic pressure, energy-system restructuring and a major public-investment shift.
en.key_risk: Larger public balance-sheet capacity fails to become physical infrastructure and productive private investment quickly enough to offset industrial restructuring, labour scarcity and higher security costs.

pt-BR.title: Alemanha: profundidade industrial exportadora, federalismo e a transição fiscal-energética da maior economia europeia
pt-BR.deck: A Alemanha mantém profundidade industrial e capacidade institucional excepcionais, mas sua transição de 2026 depende de converter mais investimento em infraestrutura, defesa e energia em produtividade enquanto emprego e demografia apertam.
pt-BR.regime: Conversão industrial sob expansão fiscal: manufatura exportadora, instituições federais e poupança profunda coexistem com emprego mais fraco, pressão demográfica, reestruturação energética e grande mudança no investimento público.
pt-BR.key_risk: A maior capacidade de balanço público não se converte em infraestrutura física e investimento privado produtivo com rapidez suficiente para compensar reestruturação industrial, escassez de trabalho e maiores custos de segurança.
